messages.subject: Statistical significance of the difference between relative entropies (categorical variable)
messages.subject_clean: Statistical significance of the difference between relative entropies (categorical variable)
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

I have a data with roughly 20 000 Finnish compound words, 10 000 of them being nouns and 10 000 adjectives. I want to know, if variation of first constituent lexemes is different in these groups, so I looked at the relative entropy (Hrel) of the distribution of their first constituent lexemes. I found out, that in the group of nouns Hrel = 0.98 and in the group of adjectives Hrel = 0.95. Next I would like to know, if the difference is statistically significant. Is there a way to test this? I have found several ways to test statistical significance of the difference when the entropy is calculated from a numerical variable, but not a single way to do it, when the entropy is calculated from a categorical variable (like I did).

For me it seems, that for once it’s really possible, that you really can’t test this statistically (but I'm kind of newbie in statistics). The only way I could think of was Fisher’s Exact Test, but I don’t know which computer could tackle that. Am I totally lost? Thank you for your help!

– Laura

messages.body_plain:
Maybe I am missing something here but what is wrong with

- either a chi-squared test for independence ( does one of the distributions differ significantly from the other?)
- or a chi-squared test for differences, where the distributions are separate rows in a table and you do a chi-squared test on the tablead a whole?

Do you have too many columns/lexemes for that?

STG
--
Stefan Th. Gries
----------------------------------
Univ. of California, Santa Barbara
http://tinyurl.com/stgries
----------------------------------

messages.subject: Final final call: bootcamps 2014
messages.body_plain:
Final final call for participation:

This year, there will be three bootcamps:

- a 4-day bootcamp on statistics for linguists with R (starting from relatively scratch but then aiming to focus on regression modeling) at the University of Mississippi, Oxford (4-7 August 2014).
- a 5-day bootcamp on corpus linguistics with R (frequency lists, concordancing, etc.) at UCSB (11-15 August 2014);
- a 5-day bootcamp on statistics for linguistics with R (introduction, mono- and multifactorial tests, and regression modeling) at UCSB (18-22 August 2014).

There are still some places available in all bootcamps so

- if you're interested in the Mississippi bootcamp, plz contact Chris Sapp (<http://home.olemiss.edu/~csapp/ <http://home.olemiss.edu/%7Ecsapp/>>);
- if you're interested in one or both of the UCSB bootcamps, plz contact Stefanie Wulff (<http://www.clas.ufl.edu/users/swulff/>).
